sections.title: The Death of Lazarus
observations: This section introduces the story of Lazarus, a close friend of Jesus, who falls ill. The delay of Jesus in coming to Lazarus highlights the theme of divine timing and purpose in suffering.
Jesus' statement that Lazarus' sickness will not end in death reveals His authority over life and death, setting the stage for the miraculous event to come.

sections.title: Jesus Comforts the Sisters
observations: Martha and Mary, Lazarus' sisters, express their grief and disappointment at Jesus' delayed arrival. Their interactions with Jesus reveal their faith and understanding of His power.
Jesus' declaration that He is the resurrection and the life emphasizes His divine identity and the hope He offers to believers, even in the face of death.

sections.title: The Raising of Lazarus
observations: This climactic moment demonstrates Jesus' power over death. His command to Lazarus to come out of the tomb illustrates His authority and the reality of resurrection.
The response of the onlookers, some believing in Jesus and others questioning Him, reflects the varied reactions to His miracles and teachings.

sections.title: The Plot to Kill Jesus
observations: The raising of Lazarus serves as a pivotal moment that intensifies the opposition against Jesus. The religious leaders' response reveals their fear of losing power and control.
This section foreshadows the eventual crucifixion of Jesus, highlighting the cost of His ministry and the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan.

importantVerses.commentary: Jesus said to her, 'I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die; and whoever lives by believing in me will never die.' This verse encapsulates the core of Christian hope in the resurrection and eternal life.
When he had said this, Jesus called in a loud voice, 'Lazarus, come out!' This moment illustrates Jesus' authority over death and serves as a powerful testament to His divine nature.

questions: What does the delay of Jesus in coming to Lazarus teach us about God's timing in our lives?
How does Jesus' statement 'I am the resurrection and the life' shape our understanding of death and eternal life?
What can we learn from the responses of Martha and Mary in their grief and faith?
How does the miracle of Lazarus foreshadow the events leading to Jesus' own death and resurrection?
